description: Teach-mode + passive coaching during history. Educational only.

modules.title: Fever history structure
points: Establish a source-focused systems review (respiratory, urinary, abdominal, skin/joint) rather than treating fever as a diagnosis on its own.
Always screen for sepsis red flags: confusion, hypotension, rapidly worsening course.
Travel, exposure, and recent antibiotic use reshape the differential significantly.

modules.title: Sepsis red flags
points: Hypotension or marked tachycardia with fever should trigger a sepsis-pathway mindset.
Early source identification and cultures precede a leisurely outpatient-style history.

Q000018.why_ask: Rigors/night sweats raise concern for bacteraemia or a focal collection.
Q000018.think: True rigors are a stronger predictor of bloodstream infection than subjective chills.

Q000053.why_ask: Travel and exposure history reshapes the infectious differential substantially.
Q000053.think: Endemic-disease and food/water-borne causes should be considered early when relevant.

Q000074.why_ask: Altered mental status with fever is a red flag for CNS infection or severe sepsis.
Q000074.think: This finding should escalate urgency regardless of the rest of the history.

answer_triggers.title: Unlocked: travel/exposure branch
points: Consider endemic infections and food/water-borne illness.
Ask about specific region, timing, and prophylaxis/vaccination.
